title: AI_Overviews
summary:
AI Overviews is an artificial intelligence feature integrated into Google Search that produces AI-generated summaries of search results. AI Overviews were first introduced as part of Google's Search Generative Experience, which was unveiled at the Google I/O conference in May 2023. In May 2024 at Google I/O 2024, the feature was rebranded as AI Overviews and launched in the United States. As of May 2025, AI Overviews are available in over 200 countries and territories, and more than 40 languages.

Researchers estimated the causal impact of Google's AI Overview on Wikipedia traffic by leveraging the feature's staggered geographic rollout. Across 161,382 matched article-language pairs, AI Overview exposure reduces daily traffic to English Wikipedia articles by approximately 15%. Total traffic from Google to Wikipedia has fallen sharply since early 2024, and the shift aligns with Google's full rollout. Wikipedia's experience has been described as "a canary in the coal mine" for the effects of AI Overviews replacing clicks.

In May 2024, Google temporarily restricted the AI tool after it provided nonsensical and harmful suggestions, such as telling users to eat rocks or apply glue on pizza. Critics argue that relying on AI-generated summaries may perpetuate inaccuracies or oversimplify complex topics, and there is apprehension about the ethical implications of AI-driven content aggregation, including its impact on intellectual property rights and the visibility of smaller content providers.

On February 24, 2025, Chegg sued Alphabet over the AI Overviews feature, claiming that it was leading to students preferring low-quality, unverified AI summaries, thus violating antitrust law. In September 2025, Penske Media Corporation, the publisher of Rolling Stone and The Hollywood Reporter, also sued Google over the feature. Google pays Wikimedia for high-speed content feeds to keep its Knowledge Graphs and AI Overviews fresh, creating a complex dynamic where Google relies heavily on Wikipedia's content while simultaneously reducing traffic to it.
